supporting_observations.claim: WS-BCARTER-01 made repeated connections to the explicit proxy at roughly five-minute intervals from 13:41 to 14:10 UTC. The supplied flow records show similar traffic volumes, but do not identify the destination hostname or originating process for most of those connections.

At 14:10:59 UTC, the proxy recorded a successful HTTPS tunnel to update.chartmate-imaging.com, and process/network records associate that connection with C:\Program Files\ChartMate\cmupdate.exe. This matches the inventory description of the approved updater and its approximately five-minute check cadence.

At 13:20 UTC, DC-HD-01 issued Kerberos tickets for lucy.park to the WS-LPARK-01$ service from WS-BCARTER-01's IP, and WS-LPARK-01 recorded a network logon for lucy.park from that same source. This cross-workstation authentication is unexplained in the supplied evidence.
At 13:58:59 UTC, WS-BCARTER-01 connected to DC-HD-01 over SMB; the DC recorded the associated logon as ANONYMOUS LOGON using NTLM. The records do not show what resource or operation was involved.

At 14:14:56 UTC, ben.carter launched Cisco AnyConnect's vpnui.exe, and a signed Cisco vpnapi.dll was loaded. The inventory says the organization has no VPN; these records show a client launch, not a successful VPN connection.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied proxy and flow records do not identify the process or hostname for most of the periodic connections; the ChartMate association is directly evidenced only for the 14:10:59 connection.
The SMB records do not identify the share, files, or action associated with the connection to DC-HD-01.
The AnyConnect process records do not establish that a VPN tunnel was created or that remote access occurred.
The supplied records do not include enough endpoint or directory audit detail to explain the lucy.park authentication to WS-LPARK-01.
claims_not_established: That every periodic proxy connection was to update.chartmate-imaging.com or was generated by cmupdate.exe.
That the lucy.park authentication was unauthorized, or that it resulted in account changes or other actions.
That the SMB connection was malicious or involved access to sensitive data.
That AnyConnect connected to a VPN or enabled remote access.
That WS-BCARTER-01 was compromised or that the observed activity was part of a coordinated malicious operation.
additional_evidence_needed: Proxy records mapping each periodic connection to its destination hostname, user, and process where available.
Endpoint process, command-line, file, and script activity on WS-BCARTER-01 around the observed authentication and SMB events.
DC-HD-01 and WS-LPARK-01 audit details for the lucy.park logon, including subsequent actions and any account or group changes.
SMB server-side audit records identifying the resource and operations associated with the connection to DC-HD-01.
AnyConnect client and network logs to determine whether a tunnel was attempted or established.
